claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology published Registered Reports describing how they intended to replicate selected experiments from 29 high-impact preclinical cancer biology papers published between 2010 and 2012.
source: As part of the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology, we published Registered Reports that described how we intended to replicate selected experiments from 29 high-impact preclinical cancer biology papers published between 2010 and 2012.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and describes the scope of the project.

evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and describes the outcomes of completed replications.

claim: PC9 cells exposed to 2 µM erlotinib for 9 days resulted in ~6% of cells remaining viable and continuing to proliferate.

evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: The original study by Sharma et al., 2010 reported ~0.3% of PC9 cells remained viable after erlotinib treatment.

evidence: This is a citation to the original study results.

evidence: This is stated as a confirmed finding in the replication attempt.

claim: Deletion in exon 19 confers EGFR TKI sensitivity.
source: We confirmed the PC9 cells used in the replication attempt had a deletion in exon 19, which confers epidermal growth factor receptor(EGFR) TKI sensitivity (Arao et al., 2004), and did not contain a T790M mutation, which has been shown to confer erlotinib resistance (Kobayashi et al., 2005; Pao et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Arao et al., 2004.

claim: The original study by Sharma et al., 2010 reported a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of ~0.0085 µM erlotinib for PC9 cell survival.
source: We also performed a survival assay (Figure 1C) and checked EGFR kinase activation (Figure 1D), which both required higher concentrations of erlotinib to achieve a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (survival: ~0.15 µM; EGFR: >1 µM) compared to what was reported in the original study (survival: ~0.0085 µM; EGFR: <0.01 µM) (Sharma et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a citation to the original study results.

claim: EGFR kinase activation required >1 µM erlotinib in the replication attempt.
source: We also performed a survival assay (Figure 1C) and checked EGFR kinase activation (Figure 1D), which both required higher concentrations of erlotinib to achieve a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (survival: ~0.15 µM; EGFR: >1 µM) compared to what was reported in the original study (survival: ~0.0085 µM; EGFR: <0.01 µM) (Sharma et al., 2010).

claim: Erlotinib hydrochloride was used in a paper that reported DTPs from PC9 cells.

claim: Glioblastoma cells transdifferentiate into tumor endothelial cells, supporting the idea that glioblastoma stem cells contribute to the endothelial angiogenic properties of these tumors.
source: It has been reported that glioblastoma cells transdifferentiate into tumor endothelial cells, supporting the idea that glioblastoma stem cells contribute to the endothelial angiogenic properties of these tumors (Ricci-Vitiani et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2010).

claim: Glioblastoma stem cells transdifferentiate into pericytes rather than endothelial cells.
source: However, it has also been reported that glioblastoma stem cells transdifferentiate into pericytes rather than endothelial cells (Cheng et al., 2013).

claim: Tie2 expression was low in glioblastoma cells compared to higher expression in endothelial cells.
source: We found that Tie2 expression was low in the glioblastoma cells compared to higher expression in endothelial cells (Figure 2A), similar to the original study.

claim: The meta-analyses for Tie2 expression were not statistically significant.
source: The meta-analyses were not statistically significant.

claim: GNAO1 has been identified as having a hypermethylated promoter region and being downregulated in hepatoma carcinoma.
source: Since then, GNAO1, which encodes the Gαo subunit of heterotrimeric guanine-binding proteins (G-proteins), has been identified as having a hypermethylated promoter region and being downregulated in colorectal cancer (Hauptman et al., 2019; Hua et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2017) and hepatoma carcinoma (Xu et al., 2018).

source: Human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs) stably expressing wild-type GNAO1 or GNAO1R243H demonstrated increased colony formation in a soft agar assay compared to both vector control and uninfected HMECs (Figure 3A, B), similar to the original study that reported 1.8 times as many colonies in GNAO1R243H expressing cells compared to wild-type GNAO1 (Kan et al., 2010).

claim: The original study by Kan et al., 2010 reported 1.8 times as many colonies in GNAO1R243H expressing cells compared to wild-type GNAO1.
source: Human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs) stably expressing wild-type GNAO1 or GNAO1R243H demonstrated increased colony formation in a soft agar assay compared to both vector control and uninfected HMECs (Figure 3A, B), similar to the original study that reported 1.8 times as many colonies in GNAO1R243H expressing cells compared to wild-type GNAO1 (Kan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a citation to the original study results.

claim: The two studies were consistent in direction for GNAO1 colony formation and the meta-analysis was statistically significant.

evidence: This is stated as a result of the meta-analysis.

claim: The R243H mutation promotes an increase in anchorage independent growth compared to cells expressing wild-type GNAO1.
source: The two studies were consistent in direction and when considering if the effect size point estimate of each study was within the 95% CI of the other study and the meta-analysis was also statistically significant, suggesting the R243H mutation promotes an increase in anchorage independent growth compared to cells expressing wild-type GNAO1.

claim: Some RAF inhibitors paradoxically activate the Ras–Raf–MEK–ERK pathway in the context of wild-type BRAF.

claim: A kinase-dead BRAF was found to induce lung adenocarcinoma.

claim: Kinase-impaired or kinase-dead (class 3) BRAF mutants are more dependent on CRAF for pathway activation and are susceptible to inhibition of activated Ras.
source: Similarly, kinase-impaired or kinase-dead (class 3) BRAF mutants were shown to be more dependent on CRAF for pathway activation and were susceptible to inhibition of activated Ras (Yao et al., 2017).

claim: In D04 cells, sorafenib and PD184352 blocked ERK activity while SB590885 did not.

claim: The original study by Heidorn et al., 2010 reported increased ERK activity in D04 cells treated with 885A, a close analog of SB590885.
